uncited: *   **SVQ Formulation:** For a vector $z \in \mathbb{R}^{ML}$, split into $M$ sub-vectors $z_m \in \mathbb{R}^L$.
*   **Base Importance Score ($\bar{I}_i$):** Determine if Gaussian $i$ is the dominant contributor for at least one ray $\rho$.
*   **Local Distinctiveness:** Approximate neighbor selection by sorting Gaussians in Morton order and selecting adjacent indices as local neighbors.
*   **Redundancy:** Naive thresholding based on blending weights can remove all similar Gaussians simultaneously or retain redundant ones.
*   **Training Overhead:** Updating indices and codes at every iteration increases training time.
